title: Trading Zones
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/0/body: With a **limit entry**, you place a buy limit order ahead of time on the demand zone's **proximal line**, with your stop loss just **past the distal line**. The upside is a better entry price and a higher risk-to-reward; the downside is that you enter **with no confirmation at all**.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/0/visu: Limit entry on the proximal line
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/0/exam: Buy limit on the proximal line
Stop loss past the distal line
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/1/body: With a **confirmation entry**, you wait for price to enter the zone and **show a reaction**, like a **bullish pin bar or engulfing**. It's a safer entry, but you get a worse price (here 1.0827 instead of 1.0812), and sometimes price leaves without you.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/2/prom: Which statement about limit entries is true?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/2/opti: Always more profitable than confirmation entries
The entry price is so good you don't need a stop loss
It only triggers after a confirmation candle closes
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/2/expl: A limit on the proximal line is the entry closest to your stop loss, so risk is smaller and relative reward bigger. But since you don't wait for price to react, you have no confirmation.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/3/prom: Gold is heading back to its fresh demand zone. Using a limit entry, where do you place your buy limit order? Drag its line.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/3/expl: With a limit entry, the buy limit sits on the zone's proximal line: the top of the base's body, around 2388. That way you get filled on price's first touch of the zone, and your stop loss goes just below the distal line (2380). Well above the zone, it's no longer a zone entry.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/4/prom: Price is back at the demand zone, and a confirmation trader is waiting for a reversal candle. Which candle gave that confirmation?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/4/expl: After two red candles inside the zone, this green candle covered the previous candle's entire body (a bullish engulfing). Buyers took control inside the zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/5/stat: With a confirmation entry, your entry price is usually worse than with a limit entry.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/5/expl: Because you wait for price to react from the zone, you buy higher and the distance to your stop loss grows. In return, you take fewer pointless entries.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/6/pair: An order placed ahead on the proximal line
Entering after price reacts in the zone
Your stop loss sits just past it
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/7/body: There's no single answer. Many traders use limits for **fresh, very strong zones** and wait for confirmation on **ordinary or counter-trend zones**. What matters is picking your method in advance and applying it **consistently**.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/7/tip: Log your method in your journal, so after 50 trades you'll know which one works better for you.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/8/prom: Price reached a fresh supply zone and formed a bearish engulfing. What does a confirmation trader expect?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/8/expl: A fresh supply zone with a bearish engulfing inside it means sellers reacted. That's the confirmation the trader was waiting for. A drop is more likely, with a stop loss above the zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/9/prom: Price reached a supply zone, but candles keep pushing up hard with no sign of a reversal. What does a confirmation trader do?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/9/opti: Stays out and waits for a signal
Sells right away because price is in the zone
Buys because the zone is sure to break
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l1/steps/9/expl: That's the whole point of a confirmation entry: if the zone doesn't react, there's no trade. Sometimes the best trade is no trade.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/0/titl: Stop loss past the distal line
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/0/body: A sensible stop loss sits just **past the distal line** of the zone, with a **safety buffer** (a few pips, say). If price breaks the distal line and closes there, the zone is broken and **the reason for the trade is gone**.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/1/body: The most common target is the **nearest opposing zone**: for a buy, the first supply zone above price. Here the target is 1.0870, so 50 pips of reward against 25 pips of risk: **1:2**. Many traders pass on anything less.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/2/prom: What's the risk-to-reward ratio of this buy trade?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/3/prom: To buy from this demand zone, which line is a sensible stop loss?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/3/expl: Line "A" is just below the zone's distal line, so it only triggers if the zone really breaks. "B" is mid-zone and "C" is even above the zone; the slightest dip into the zone would close the trade for no reason.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/4/prom: To buy from the demand zone at the bottom of the chart, the sensible target is the supply zone above. Tap that supply zone's base candle.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/4/expl: After three bullish candles, this one has a small body and the sharp drop starts right there: the base of an RBD. The supply zone on this candle is the first sensible target for the buy.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/5/stat: It's best to put your stop loss exactly on the distal line, with no buffer.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/5/expl: Price sometimes pokes a little past the distal line and comes back (because of spread or noise). A small buffer past the distal line keeps the trade from closing for no reason.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/6/prom: You sold from this supply zone's proximal line (150.33). Place your stop loss just above the zone's distal line.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/6/expl: A supply zone's distal line is the base's highest wick, here 150.60. Your stop loss sits a few pips above it as a buffer (say 150.65 to 150.70). Inside the zone, a normal poke would take you out; much further away just adds needless risk.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/7/sent: When buying from a demand zone, your stop loss goes just ___ the distal line and your target on the nearest ___ zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/7/expl: Your stop loss belongs where a break of the zone is proven (below the distal line), and your target where sellers will probably step in again (the supply zone).
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/8/prom: Put the steps for planning a buy from a demand zone in order.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/8/item: Mark the zone and its proximal and distal lines
Put your stop loss just below the distal line
If it's at least 1:2, place the order
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/8/expl: First you lay out the trade (zone, stop loss, target), then you check whether it's worth it. Placing the order always comes last.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/9/prom: The next supply zone starts at 1.0840. Do you take this buy trade?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/9/opti: No; the reward to the supply zone is less than the risk
Yes; every demand zone is worth buying
Yes, as long as you remove the stop loss
Yes, because the reward is 45 pips
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l2/steps/9/expl: The reward to the supply zone is only 20 pips (1.0840 − 1.0820), but the risk is 25 pips. Anything under 1:1 isn't worth the risk.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/0/body: If a candle closes with its **body past the distal line**, the zone is **broken** and no longer valid for trades in the old direction. A strong break of a supply zone means buyers absorbed all the sell orders there.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/1/body: A supply zone that broke to the upside with force may act as **demand** when price comes back (and vice versa), just like resistance turning into support. Many traders call this area a **flip zone**.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/2/prom: Which candle really broke the supply zone? Tap it.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/2/expl: This is the first candle whose body closed above the zone's distal line. The green candle before only pierced the zone with its wick and closed below it, so that doesn't count as a break.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/3/stat: If only a candle's wick pokes past a supply zone's distal line and the body closes lower, the zone is definitely broken.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/3/expl: A wick means price went there and got rejected. The usual test for a break is a body close past the distal line; a wick poking through is more a sign that some of the orders got used up.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/4/prom: A supply zone broke with a strong candle, and now price has come back to that area. What role does this area probably play?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/4/opti: Irrelevant; it has no role now
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/4/expl: Buyers absorbed this area's sell orders and closed above it. Many traders expect it to act as demand when price returns.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/5/prom: The old supply zone (gray) broke to the upside with a strong candle, and price is coming back. To buy from the flip zone, where do you put your buy limit?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/5/expl: The broken supply zone can now act as demand. Price is coming back from above, so its first touch is the zone's upper edge (around 1.0862). A buy limit between the upper edge and the middle of the zone makes sense, with a stop loss just below the zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/6/prom: Price came back to the flip zone and formed a hammer. Which move is more likely?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/6/expl: The old supply broke with force, price is back for the first time, and the hammer shows buyers defending this area. Continuation up is more likely; stop loss below the zone.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/7/prom: You bought from a demand zone with your stop loss just below the distal line. Price closed below the distal line with a strong candle. What does that mean?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/7/opti: The reason for the trade is gone, and the stop loss did its job
The zone got stronger, so you should add to the position
Move your stop loss lower so you don't take a loss
The zone is still fresh, so it's fine
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/7/expl: A close below the distal line means the zone is broken: exactly the scenario your stop loss was there for. Moving it only makes the loss bigger.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/8/prom: Put the events of a bullish flip in order.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/8/item: A candle closes above the distal line
Price returns to the broken zone
Buy with a stop loss below the zone
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/8/expl: First the zone has to exist and truly break; then price comes back and reacts bullishly, and the entry comes last of all.
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/9/prom: A daily supply zone broke with a strong candle. Price came back to it for the first time and formed a bullish pin bar. The next supply zone is three times your stop distance away. How's this setup?
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/9/opti: High quality: a fresh flip, confirmation and 1:3 reward
Weak: a broken zone has no role anymore
Weak: you should sell off that supply zone
High quality, so no stop loss needed
lessons/supply-demand-u3-l3/steps/9/expl: Every box is ticked: a strong break, the first return, a confirmation candle and a reward of 3x the risk. But even the best setup can fail, so you always need a stop loss.
